title: Watercress-Apple Yuja Salad
shortDescription: Peppery watercress and crisp apple are tossed just before service with a bright commercial yuja-cheong vinaigrette.
culturalContext: This is a contemporary salad pairing Korean yuja preserve with watercress and apple; it is not presented as a canonical Korean dish. The Korean display name is a descriptive transliteration pending language review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

instructions.heading: Inspect produce
instructions.action: Discard slimy, bruised, or moldy watercress and apple; wash hands and clean the work area.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep ready-to-eat produce separate from raw meat and seafood.

instructions.heading: Wash under running water
instructions.action: Rinse watercress and apple under cool running water without soap or produce wash.
instructions.safetyNote: Washing reduces surface contamination but does not sterilize produce.

instructions.heading: Dry thoroughly
instructions.action: Spin or pat watercress dry with clean single-use or freshly laundered towels.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean equipment reserved from raw-food preparation.

instructions.heading: Mix dressing
instructions.action: Shake yuja-cheong, vinegar, oils, and salt in a clean jar.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Dressing is emulsified and label-listed allergens are confirmed.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean spoon and verify the yuja-cheong label.

instructions.heading: Cut apple
instructions.action: Core and thinly slice the washed apple on a clean board.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices are even with seeds and core removed.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a stable cutting surface and a clean knife.

instructions.heading: Toss and serve
instructions.action: Toss watercress and apple with dressing immediately before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Leaves are lightly coated, not wilted.
instructions.safetyNote: Serve promptly; discard salad left above 40°F / 4°C beyond 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

grillSetup: No grill required; prepare only on cleaned and sanitized ready-to-eat surfaces.
visualDonenessCues: Apple has no bruised or moldy areas
Salad is lightly coated immediately before service
foodSafetyNotes: Wash produce under running water; do not use soap, detergent, or bleach.
Use clean tools and keep ready-to-eat produce away from raw meat and seafood.
Verify the commercial yuja-cheong label for allergens and damaged seals.
Keep prepared salad cold and observe the 2-hour limit, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Verify every packaged-ingredient label and segregate tools for diners with allergies.

substitutions: Asian pear may replace apple after washing and coring.
A verified sesame-free neutral oil may replace sesame oil.
ingredientSourcing: Choose crisp watercress without slime or yellowing.
Use commercial yuja-cheong from an intact package and verify its label.
makeAhead: Wash and dry watercress and mix dressing up to 1 day ahead; store separately and cut apple near service.
storage: Refrigerate components separately at or below 40°F / 4°C; use tossed salad the same day.
leftovers: Discard dressed salad after extended service; undressed, uncontaminated components may remain refrigerated for 1 day.
servingSuggestions: Toss at the table just before eating.
Serve with rich grilled meat or seafood.

faq.question: Can I wash watercress with soap?
faq.answer: No. Rinse produce under running water and use clean hands and tools.

faq.question: Can I dress it early?
faq.answer: Keep the dressing separate until service for texture and cold-control quality.

metaDescription: Toss crisp watercress and apple with a bright yuja dressing using clean ready-to-eat tools, label checks, running-water washing, and cold holding.
